Class IO<A>

java.lang.Object
forj.effect.IO<A>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Kind<IO,A>
public abstract sealed class IO<A> extends Object implements Kind<IO,A>
A lazy, re-runnable description of a computation that may perform side effects, fail, or wait: cats-effect 2's IO, on virtual threads.

Nothing happens until unsafeRunSync(), and each run starts over. The interpreter is a loop with an explicit stack, so long flatMap chains (recursive loops written with flatMap) don't overflow the Java stack. Blocking inside delay is fine: runs and fibers are virtual threads. Cancelling a fiber interrupts its thread; the interpreter checks for interruption between steps and fails with InterruptedException, so bracket releases still run.

IO is its own witness: IO<A> is a Kind<IO, A>, and its instance, concurrent, provides the whole ladder up to ConcurrentEffect.
